headline: Deep learning models predict protein binding, solubility, stability and design fitness
label: Deep Learning Biomolecular Prediction
summary: Graph, attention, and language-model architectures are now benchmarked against physics and experimental data for prediction and design.
synthesis: The common thread is deep learning applied to biomolecular prediction and design, with architectures ranging from edge-aware graph attention networks and protein language model embeddings to diffusion-based structure generation. Several entries integrate physics rather than replacing it: ARID-sf combines force fields with structural features and language model embeddings for antibody-antigen docking ranking, while ProteinMPNN and ThermoMPNN are tested as candidate replacements for umbrella sampling of troponin C free energies, reporting R2 0.82. Others emphasize benchmarking against established predictors, as in the StructureDCA evaluation on CYP2C9 variants and the AlphaMissense comparison for hemoglobin pathogenicity. ProteinDPO applies direct preference optimization to a structure-conditioned language model for fitness-aligned design. The diffusion review highlights validation criteria and thermodynamic challenges, and the hybrid AI-physics perspective addresses interface scoring limits. A recurring contribution is evaluation against physical and experimental criteria rather than predictive accuracy alone.
